stem: In science, work is said to be done when a __________ moves an object.
solution: Work is done when a force acts on an object and moves it in the direction of the force.

stem: Work done is calculated as __________.
options: force × displacement (in the direction of force)
solution: Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force.

stem: The SI unit of work is the __________.
solution: Work is measured in joules (J); one joule is one newton-metre.

stem: One joule of work is done when a force of __________ moves an object by 1 metre in its direction.
solution: 1 joule = 1 newton × 1 metre; a 1 N force moving an object 1 m does 1 J of work.

stem: If a person holds a heavy bag stationary, the work done on the bag is __________.
solution: No displacement means no work is done, even though a force is applied.

stem: The capacity to do work is called __________.
solution: Energy is the capacity or ability to do work.

stem: The SI unit of energy is the __________.
solution: Energy, like work, is measured in joules (J).

stem: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called __________ energy.
solution: Kinetic energy is the energy of a body due to its motion.

stem: The kinetic energy of a body is given by __________.
solution: Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × velocity² (½ mv²).

stem: The energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration is called __________ energy.
solution: Potential energy is stored energy due to position or configuration.

stem: The gravitational potential energy of a body at height h is given by __________.
solution: Gravitational potential energy = mass × gravity × height (mgh).

stem: A stretched bow or a compressed spring stores __________ energy.
solution: A stretched bow or compressed spring stores elastic potential energy.

stem: The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be __________.
solution: The law of conservation of energy: energy is neither created nor destroyed but only changes from one form to another.

stem: A body falling from a height converts its __________ into kinetic energy.
solution: As a body falls, its gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy.

stem: In a simple pendulum, energy continuously changes between __________.
solution: A pendulum's energy changes between kinetic (at the bottom) and potential (at the extremes) energy.

stem: The rate of doing work (or the rate of energy transfer) is called __________.
solution: Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.

stem: The SI unit of power is the __________.
solution: Power is measured in watts (W); one watt is one joule per second.

stem: Power is calculated as __________.
solution: Power = work done ÷ time taken.

stem: 1 kilowatt is equal to __________ watts.
solution: 1 kilowatt = 1000 watts.

stem: The commercial unit of electrical energy is the __________.
solution: The kilowatt-hour (kWh), or 'unit', is the commercial unit of electrical energy.

stem: 1 kilowatt-hour equals __________ joules.
A device that makes work easier is called a __________.
solution: A machine is a device that makes work easier, faster, or changes the direction of a force.

stem: A lever, an inclined plane and a pulley are examples of __________.
solution: Levers, inclined planes and pulleys are simple machines.

stem: A see-saw is an example of a __________.
solution: A see-saw is a lever, with a fixed pivot (fulcrum) in the middle.

stem: The fixed point about which a lever turns is called the __________.
solution: The fulcrum is the fixed pivot point about which a lever rotates.

stem: A ramp used to move heavy loads to a higher level is an example of a(n) __________.
solution: A ramp is an inclined plane, which reduces the effort needed to raise a load.

stem: A pulley changes the __________ of the force needed to lift a load.
solution: A single fixed pulley changes the direction of the applied force, making lifting more convenient.

stem: Simple machines are useful because they __________.
options: reduce the effort or change the direction of force needed
solution: Simple machines make work easier by reducing effort or changing the direction of the applied force; they do not create energy.

stem: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 3 m/s has kinetic energy of __________.
solution: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

stem: A 5 kg object raised to a height of 2 m (g = 10 m/s²) gains potential energy of __________.
The energy stored in food and fuels is a form of __________ energy.
solution: Food and fuels store chemical energy, released during reactions like respiration or burning.

stem: When we switch on a bulb, electrical energy is converted mainly into __________.
solution: A bulb converts electrical energy into light and heat energy.

stem: The energy released in the Sun and stars is __________ energy.
solution: The Sun and stars release nuclear energy from nuclear reactions.

stem: A device with a machine 'advantage' can lift a heavy load with a smaller effort but over a __________.
solution: A simple machine may reduce effort but the effort must act over a larger distance; total work stays about the same.

stem: No work is done when the force applied is __________ to the direction of displacement.
solution: When the force is perpendicular to the displacement, no work is done (e.g., carrying a bag horizontally).

stem: The energy of a moving car is mainly __________ energy.
solution: A moving car possesses kinetic energy due to its motion.

stem: The energy of water stored in a high dam is mainly __________ energy.
solution: Water at a height in a dam has gravitational potential energy, which can be converted to electricity.

stem: In a hydroelectric power plant, the potential energy of water is converted into __________.
options: kinetic energy and then electrical energy
solution: Falling water's potential energy becomes kinetic energy that turns turbines to generate electrical energy.

stem: Two persons do the same work; the one taking less time has __________ power.
solution: Power = work/time, so doing the same work in less time means more power.

stem: A screw and an axe (wedge) are examples of __________.
solution: A screw is a type of inclined plane, and a wedge/axe is a simple machine.

stem: Which of the following possesses potential energy?
solution: A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy; the others show kinetic energy.

stem: Energy transformations always obey the law of conservation of energy, meaning the total energy __________.
solution: In any transformation, the total energy remains constant; it only changes form.

stem: A crane lifting a load does work against __________.
solution: Lifting a load upward does work against the force of gravity.

stem: The power of a machine rated 100 W means it does __________ of work each second.
solution: 100 W means 100 joules of work is done every second.

stem: Which of the following is a form of energy?
solution: Heat is a form of energy; displacement, mass and time are not forms of energy.

stem: When work is done against friction, energy is mostly converted into __________.
solution: Work done against friction is largely converted into heat energy.

stem: A wheel and axle (like a steering wheel) is a simple machine that helps by __________.
options: applying a small effort over a larger turn to move a load
solution: A wheel and axle lets a small effort applied on the wheel move a load on the axle more easily.

stem: The energy possessed by a body due to its position is __________ energy.
solution: Potential energy is due to position or configuration.

stem: A simple machine like a lever helps by __________.
options: making work easier or changing the direction of force
solution: Simple machines make work easier or change the direction of the applied force; they do not create energy.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Work, Energy, and Simple Machines' is that:
options: work is force times displacement, energy is the capacity to do work and is conserved, and simple machines make work easier
work is done even without displacement
solution: The chapter explains work, kinetic and potential energy, the conservation of energy, power, and how simple machines make work easier.

stem: Work is said to be done when a force acting on a body produces __________ in it.
solution: Work is done when a force causes displacement in its own direction.

stem: Work done is calculated as force multiplied by __________.
options: displacement in the direction of force
solution: Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force.

stem: One joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton moves a body by __________ in its direction.
If the displacement is perpendicular to the force, the work done is __________.
solution: When displacement is perpendicular to the force, work done is zero.

stem: The kinetic energy of a body is given by the formula __________.
solution: Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × velocity² (½mv²).

stem: The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor __________.
solution: Energy can only be transformed from one form to another; it is never created or destroyed.

stem: When a ball is thrown up, its kinetic energy is gradually converted into __________ energy.
solution: As the ball rises, its kinetic energy converts into potential energy.

stem: The rate of doing work is called __________.
solution: Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.

stem: One watt is equal to one joule per __________.
solution: 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

stem: The commercial unit of electrical energy, the kilowatt-hour, equals __________ joules.
A device that makes work easier by changing the direction or magnitude of a force is a __________.
solution: A simple machine changes the magnitude or direction of an applied force.

stem: A ramp used to move loads to a height is an example of an __________.
solution: An inclined plane (ramp) reduces the effort needed to raise a load.

stem: A pulley is used to __________ a load.
solution: A pulley changes the direction of the applied force, making lifting easier.

stem: The efficiency of a machine is always __________ 100% because of friction.
solution: Real machines lose energy to friction, so efficiency is always less than 100%.

stem: Food gives us energy in the form of __________ energy.
solution: Food stores chemical energy, which the body releases through respiration.

stem: The energy stored in a stretched bow is __________ energy.
solution: A stretched bow stores elastic potential energy.

stem: In a hydroelectric power plant, the __________ energy of falling water is converted to electricity.
solution: The potential and kinetic energy of falling water drive turbines to generate electricity.

stem: If a body moves in the direction of the applied force, the work done is __________.
solution: Work is positive when displacement is in the direction of the force.

stem: If the force acts opposite to the displacement, the work done is __________.
solution: Work is negative when the force opposes the displacement, as with friction.

stem: Doubling the speed of a moving body increases its kinetic energy by a factor of __________.
solution: Kinetic energy is proportional to v², so doubling speed quadruples the kinetic energy.

stem: The sum of kinetic and potential energy of a body is its __________ energy.
solution: Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic and potential energy.

stem: No work is done when a person holds a heavy load stationary because there is no __________.
solution: Without displacement, no work is done, even though a force is applied.
